findings.title: Missing prisma import causes runtime ReferenceError
findings.body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts calls prisma.credential.update at line 96 but never imports prisma. Every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService via getClient will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce event operations. Add import prisma from "@calcom/prisma".

findings.title: Stores Zod SafeParse wrapper instead of token data
findings.body: File packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 97-101 assigns const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) which returns a Zod SafeParse result { success, data, error }, then persists that wrapper as credential.key. The credential in the DB will become { success: true, data: {...} } instead of the Google tokens, so subsequent googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails and calendar sync breaks. It should persist key.data.

findings.title: Minimum token schema is invalid and destroys tokens
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts defines minimumTokenResponseSchema with computed keys [z.string().toString()] which do not create a catch-all; zod will strip all unknown fields like expires_in/expiry_date/instance_url. Callers then persist only access_token. Worse, lines 25-27 inject refresh_token = "refresh_token" literal when missing, overwriting the real refresh token preservation logic (e.g. Google, Salesforce) with a dummy value that will be saved to the DB and permanently break future refreshes.

findings.title: Sync path returns raw fetch Response incompatible with callers
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns a fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google expects res.data (GaxiosResponse), HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object, Zoho-Bigin/ZohoCRM expect axios { data }, Office365 expects fetch Response. For example Google does const token = res?.data then token.access_token which will be undefined/throw when res is a fetch Response because fetch bodies must be read via .json(). There is no response.ok check, no .json() normalization, and no shared contract, so enabling sync crashes refresh for most providers.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as userId to credential sync
findings.body: File packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts line 85-94 calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) where the third parameter is defined as userId: number | null. It sends the credential primary key as calcomUserId to the external sync endpoint, so the self-hosted endpoint will look up the wrong user and return tokens for the wrong account or fail.

findings.title: Webhook lacks method check and crashes on invalid input
findings.body: File apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts handler accepts any HTTP method (GET/PUT/DELETE) with no req.method guard, and calls zod .parse at line 31 and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) at line 57 without try/catch. Any malformed body, wrong appSlug payload, or wrong encryption key throws uncaught and returns 500 instead of 400, and can be probed via GET. It should restrict to POST and return 400 on validation/decryption failure.

findings.title: Credential upsert can overwrite wrong credential
findings.body: File apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 62-70 finds credential with findFirst where userId + appId only, ignoring type and team credentials. Users can have multiple credentials for the same appId with different types (e.g. google_calendar vs google_video, office365_calendar vs office365_video, tandem/webex/zoom duplicates). The webhook will arbitrarily update the first row and never update type, corrupting the other integration. It should filter by type or handle multiples explicitly.

findings.title: Expiry check mixes seconds and milliseconds
findings.body: File packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts line 56 defines isExpired as expiryDate < Math.round(+new Date()) where +new Date() is milliseconds, but expiry_date is stored in seconds in the callback (Math.round(+new Date()/1000 + expires_in)) and in milliseconds after refresh (Date.now() + expires_in*1000). Comparing seconds to ms means stored credentials always look expired, forcing a refresh on every meeting create/update and risking rate-limiting or loops when sync endpoint is enabled.
